secondary_c5_inspection.finding: secondary_c5_evasion.jsonl is NOT a source-authored (unchanged-text) arm candidate pool. All 5 records have source_prompt != candidate_prompt (confirmed by direct comparison) and are transformation_family 'reduced_cue_source_rewrite' - the same AI-reworded transformation used for c_paired. They are, in fact, already present in candidate_records_v2.jsonl with c_construction == 'c_paired' and inclusion_decision == 'secondary_only'. This file appears to be an evasion-flagged EXPORT/VIEW of 5 already-existing c_paired candidates that scored evasion_dominant=True, not a distinct source or a distinct construction type. It should not be confused with, or treated as progress toward, the c_source_authored arm. Its absence from summary.json is consistent with it being a byproduct/export rather than a tracked pipeline stage.

SimpleSafetyTests and SORRY-Bench access verification (flagged unresolved in 3A0) remains unresolved - out of scope for this milestone's acquire list (StrongREJECT, HarmBench, AdvBench, JBB-Behaviors only), carried forward to a future milestone.

AdvBench's literature-documented internal near-duplicate/templating pattern is not cleared by this session's exact-text-only dedup (520/520 unique strings); an embedding-based near-dup pass is still needed before any low-similarity-tail sampling from AdvBench.

StrongREJECT's raw CSV has no persistent per-row ID field; any future disjointness/overlap check must continue to use content-hash identity (as this session did), not a literal upstream 'source_id' string, since no such upstream ID exists.

The 158-row StrongREJECT disjoint/unused pool skews heavily toward 'Sexual content' (50/158, 32%) and 'Violence' (54/158, 34%) categories relative to 'Illegal goods and services' (38/158) and smaller categories. No sampling or selection decision was made this session, but a future milestone building a source-authored slice should be aware of this category imbalance before drawing from the pool.

src/diagnostics/classify_source_provenance.py is a heuristic screening tool (same category of tool as score_lexical_risk_cues.py, with the same documented limits). Its low-confidence 'complete_user_facing_prompt (imperative fallback)' classifications - 20 in StrongREJECT, 11 in HarmBench-standard, 37 in AdvBench-goal - are ambiguous imperative sentences that a human reviewer should re-check before any of this feeds a future candidate or review file.
No reusable candidate-vs-Quadrant-A contamination check exists in the pipeline tooling (gap already noted in 3A0, still open); this session's HarmBench<->QuadrantA comparison was ad hoc.
